title: Request-localized prefix merge and occupancy-aware KV slimming
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our GPU-resident KV store for prefix caches is growing with redundant, near-duplicate prefix fragments across many requests. This increases GPU memory pressure and leads to higher slot reclamation overhead during busy loads. Existing dedupe strategies operate at shard or global compaction intervals and either cause spikes in CPU/GPU activity or miss short-lived cross-request reuse opportunities.

Goal: Create a request-localized merge step that runs as part of the continuous-batching pipeline to (1) reduce duplicate prefix fragments held in GPU slabs by merging highly similar prefix fragments at microbatch time, (2) apply occupancy-aware slimming to the merged fragments so they consume fewer slots on GPU, and (3) coordinate admission/eviction with an inexpensive ghost-entry ledger to reduce churn. Solution should integrate with ongoing continuous batching (no added per-request latency >2ms on p50), and improve effective GPU KV utilization by >=15% on representative workloads without degrading model output quality by >0.5% (per prompt-set eval).
acceptance_criteria: Background microbench shows >=15% reduction in GPU KV slot occupancy across simulated multi-tenant conversational workload (mixed-short + long prompts)
P95 end-to-end token-serving latency increase <= 3ms after enabling request-localized merging under 80% GPU utilization
Regression testing shows <=0.5% change in generation token distribution / completion accuracy on core eval prompts
End-to-end integration tests added and green in CI with no flakes >2% over 24-hour run
Feature gate implemented to toggle request-local merge and ghost ledger independently
implementation_plan: Design micromerge: detect high-similarity prefix fragments within a microbatch using a lightweight sim-hash and cluster; construct ephemeral merged fragment and compute compacted KV representation
Occupancy-aware slimming: encode merged fragment with run-length token offsets and small quantized deltas when applicable (optimizations for short LLM token segments)
Admission / ghost ledger: maintain a small per-GPU ghost table (LRU+frequency hints) to avoid re-admitting recently evicted fragments; ghost entries are small (8 bytes key + 1 byte meta)
Batch integration: hook micromerge at batching boundary before KV lookups so multiple requests in same microbatch reuse merged keys without additional lookups
Fallback and safety: if merged fragment fails cold-path checksum or size budget, fall back to original per-request fragments and emit metric for analysis
Phased rollout: internal canary -> alpha with small % of traffic -> beta (dedicated capacity customers) -> full enabled for hosted with feature gate and operator override
Telemetry: add metrics for merged-fragment hit-rate, ghost-hit-rate, average fragment size pre/post, eviction churn, and model-quality deltas tied to prompt-sets
design_decisions: Run micromerge inside the batching worker to reuse already-allocated CPU cycles rather than scheduling a separate background compaction job
Use sim-hash (64-bit) with configurable distance threshold to cluster fragments: low compute cost and amenable to SIMD optimizations
Keep merged-fragment residency time short (order seconds by default) to avoid long-tail memory retention; rely on ghost ledger to reduce oscillation
Favor a write-through model for merged fragments when they are admitted to GPU KV so that eviction logic and refcounts remain unified with existing slab allocator
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Excessive CPU overhead at very high batch rates. Mitigation: adaptive sampling of microbatches (only run merge when unique-prefix density > threshold), and offload heavy clustering to a lightweight approximate path.
Risk: Incorrect merging could alter model outputs. Mitigation: conservative similarity thresholds for initial rollout and automated prompt-set regressions; allow quick rollback via feature gate.
Risk: Ghost-table may grow and itself use meaningful GPU memory. Mitigation: keep ghost table CPU-only with compacted keys and TTL-based eviction; size-capped per GPU.
Risk: Interaction with global compaction jobs causing duplicate work. Mitigation: add compaction metadata stamps so background compactors skip recently micro-merged fragments
notes: This ticket builds on prior work on incremental KV shadow checkpoints and probabilistic prefix compaction. Avoid reusing identical names or approach from those tickets; this one emphasizes microbatch-time merging and a small ghost ledger instead of global indexing.
experiments_and_results: Local perf run (dev cluster, 4xA100): mixed-convo workload: baseline KV occupancy 72GB -> post-merge 59GB (18% reduction), CPU overhead +4% overall, p95 latency +1.6ms
Quality check: run against canonical prompt suite (2000 prompts) showed token-level distribution delta 0.23% and ROUGE-like completeness delta 0.18% — within target
Failure mode observed: pathological workloads with many highly similar but non-identical prefixes caused micromerge churn; added hysteresis and sampling to mitigate
testing_plan: Unit tests for sim-hash clusterer and merged-fragment serializer
Integration test that simulates microbatch with N=128 and asserts merged-fragment reuse across requests in same batch
End-to-end A/B on dedicated capacity: 1% traffic for 48 hours, collect metrics and regression signals
Chaos test: force background compaction and run micromerge simultaneously to ensure compactor skip stamps work
